transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. 

Um... I'm a little embarrassed to even say this, because I don't want you to think badly of me or think I'm, you know, crazy or anything. I'm sure it's just from working too many hours at the shop—I'm a mechanic—but... well, the reason I'm here is... I keep hearing this man's voice. 

It usually comes from the garage vents, or sometimes right from under the hood when I'm working. It's as clear as somebody standing right next to me. And, um, he keeps telling me not to trust my husband... or he'll tell me not to touch certain cars. 

I know exactly how that sounds, but it's probably just stress playing tricks on me, right? I hope I'm explaining that okay.
Does the voice tell you what to do, or does it just give you advice or opinions?

Um, well, like I was just saying, it's mostly him... telling me not to trust my husband, or he'll specifically say not to touch certain cars. So I guess he is kind of telling me what to do. 

But I promise I don't let it mess up my work or anything! I really try my best to just ignore him when he starts talking from the vents or from under the hood. It's just hard sometimes because he sounds as clear as you and I talking right now. 

I just wanted to be completely honest with you about what he says, even though it's really embarrassing. I hope it doesn't make me sound too crazy, admitting that I hear that. Did I answer your question okay?
Does the voice ever tell you to do something that you feel you must do?

Oh, um... no, definitely not. I mean, he says those things about the cars or my husband, but... I don't feel like I actually *have* to obey him or anything. I'm always in control of what I do, I promise. 

I would never let it make me do something bad or, you know, actually stop working. I just... I really just try to tune it out and go about my day like normal. I wouldn't ever act on it. Does that make sense? I hope that's what you were asking.
Does the voice ever stop, or is it always talking to you when it's present?

Um, it's not always there, no. I mean, it's just like I mentioned before—it's mostly when I'm at the shop, you know? Like when I hear him coming from the garage vents, or... or when I'm working under the hood of a car. 

When he does talk, he just repeats those same things, telling me not to trust my husband or warning me away from certain cars. But then he stops, and it's quiet again. I don't hear him all day every day or anything like that. It's just... in those specific moments. 

I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details. Is that helpful?
How do you feel when you hear the voice talking to you?

Um... well, I guess it just makes me feel... a little uncomfortable? Like, it's weird, obviously, hearing something when you're just trying to work. But I promise it doesn't upset me too much! I mostly just feel... maybe a bit distracted for a second, but then I just shake it off. 

I don't want you to think I'm sitting there terrified or, you know, unable to do my job, because I'm really not. I just take a deep breath and get right back to the cars. I handle it pretty well, I think. Does that sound like I'm managing it okay? I just really want to make sure I'm doing the right things to get better.
Does hearing the voice affect your relationship with your husband or anyone else in your life?

Um... well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, every couple has disagreements, right? It's really not that bad, I promise. But... I guess recently the fighting at home did get a little intense. Just because I've been a bit distracted, I think. It actually got bad enough that my husband... well, he brought me in for an emergency evaluation. But I know he just did it because he cares about me! I'm not mad at him or anything, we're going to be totally fine.

And, um, as for other people... at the shop... I might have made a couple of small mistakes lately. Nothing terrible! But people were just a little worried about me being safe, so they actually pulled me off the high-voltage EV work for now. Which is completely fine, I totally agree with them putting safety first, and I told them that. I'm still doing great with the regular repairs. 

I really am trying my hardest to keep everything together and not let it cause problems. I want to be a good wife and a good mechanic. Does it sound like I'm doing the right things to get past this?
Does the voice ever give you commands or instructions that are directed at you and no one else?

Um... commands? No, no, he never tells me to do bad things or anything scary like that, I promise! It's just... well, like I said before, it's that man's voice. I hear him clear as day, like he's standing right next to me, coming from the vents or under the hood. 

And he just... he tells me not to trust my husband, or he warns me not to touch certain cars. That's really all it is. Just... instructions like that, I guess. But I don't always listen to him! I try to just do my job and go home. I really don't want you to think I'm doing crazy things because of it. I'm safe, and I'm trying so hard to be cooperative. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm answering right.
Do you ever find it hard to express your thoughts or get your words mixed up when the voice is talking to you?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, maybe if he starts talking right when a customer or one of the other mechanics is asking me a question, I might just... you know, pause for a second. Just to make sure I'm focusing on the real person. But I definitely don't get my words mixed up or anything like that, I promise! 

I can always explain the repairs and talk to everyone at the shop perfectly fine. I really try hard to make sure I'm always speaking clearly so nobody gets the wrong idea or worries about me. Actually... am I making sense to you right now? I hope I'm explaining everything okay. I just want to make sure I'm giving you good answers so you can help me.
Do you feel anxious when you hear the voice talking to you?

Um... anxious? No, I don't think so. I really try hard not to let it get to me, you know? 

I mean, maybe it's just a tiny bit startling if it happens right when I'm under a hood and not expecting it, but I definitely don't panic or get all worked up, I promise! I just take a deep breath and try to stay as calm as I can. I really don't want to overreact and make things harder for my husband or the guys at the shop. I just try to brush it off and keep smiling. 

I hope that's a good way to handle it? I just want to make sure I'm reacting the right way so I can get better.
Do you ever have trouble organizing your thoughts or making sense when you're not hearing the voice?

Um... no, no, definitely not. I think my thoughts are always pretty clear, honestly. 

I mean, I can always figure out what's wrong with a car and explain it to the customer without any problems. I'm really careful to make sure I'm always making sense, you know? I don't want anyone to think I'm confused or can't handle my job. I write down all my repair notes perfectly fine, and my husband never says anything about me not making sense. 

I really try to stay sharp and focused all the time. I'm doing okay with that, right? I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the right impression.
Is the voice always present when you're at the shop, or does it come and go?

Um... it kind of comes and goes, I think. It's not like he's talking to me every single second I'm at work. 

But... well, I guess it happens enough that I had to come see you. It's just... I keep hearing this man's voice. And it sounds like it's coming right out of the garage vents, or sometimes even from under the hood of the car I'm working on. It's so clear, it's honestly like there's somebody standing right next to me. 

And he... he tells me things. Like, he tells me not to trust my husband, which is awful because my husband is so good to me. Or he'll tell me not to touch certain cars. I try really hard to just ignore him and do my job anyway, because I don't want to let anyone down. I know it sounds a little crazy, but I'm really trying to handle it the best I can. Is it... is it okay that I'm telling you all this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details so we can fix it.
Does the voice ever say anything mean or critical about you?

Um... mean things? Oh, no, not really. I mean, he's never really said anything bad about *me* personally. 

He mostly just talks about the cars or... or my husband, like I mentioned. He doesn't insult me or call me names or anything like that, I promise. I try really hard to be a good person and do my job right, so I don't think there'd be much for him to criticize anyway, you know? If he did say something mean, I'd probably just try to brush it off and focus on my work. I wouldn't want to let it bother me. 

So, no, he's not mean to me. That's a good thing, right? I hope that means it's not as bad as it could be.
Do you ever see things that aren't really there when you're alone or in a quiet space?

Um... see things? Oh, no. No, definitely not. I don't see anything that isn't supposed to be there, I promise. 

It's really just... well, like I was saying earlier, it's just that man's voice. The one coming from the garage vents or under the hood. I hear him as clear as if he were standing right beside me, telling me not to trust my husband or to stay away from certain cars, but I never actually *see* anyone there. 

I always double-check, too, just to be sure, because I want to be thorough and do a good job. But my eyes are perfectly fine. I wouldn't want you to think I'm, you know, seeing ghosts or completely losing my grip. It's just the hearing part that brought me in. That means I'm not doing too badly, right? Like, it's a good sign that I don't see things? I just really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so I can get back on track.
Do you ever have trouble finding the right words when you're talking to someone?

Um... finding the right words? No, I don't think so. I mean, I try really hard to be clear when I'm talking to people, especially customers at the shop or... or you, of course. 

Sometimes I might pause for a second just to make sure I'm saying the right thing, because I want to be helpful and not waste anyone's time. But I don't get confused or lose my words or anything like that. I can always explain what's wrong with a car or what needs fixing. 

I'm doing okay explaining things to you today, aren't I? I really hope I'm making sense and giving you what you need. I just want to be as cooperative as possible.
Is the voice talking to you right now?

Um... right now? No, no, he's not talking right now. It's nice and quiet in here, which is a relief. 

Like I was mentioning before, it's really just when I'm at work... you know, I'll be working on a car, and I'll hear him so clearly coming from the garage vents, or sometimes right from under the hood when I'm checking an engine. And it's always just him telling me things like... like I shouldn't trust my husband, or that I need to stay away from certain cars. But he's definitely not here in your office. 

I wouldn't bring that into your space, I promise. I'm really trying to just focus on our conversation and be a good patient. It's okay that I only hear him at the shop, right? That's probably better than hearing him everywhere, isn't it?
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are disjointed or hard to put into words when you're not hearing the voice?

Um... no, I don't think my thoughts get jumbled or anything like that. I really try to stay organized, you know? Like, when I'm working on a transmission or explaining a repair to a customer, I have to be clear, and I always am. 

Even when I'm not at the shop and it's quiet, my mind feels pretty normal. I mean, I might get a little distracted sometimes, just thinking about all the things I need to get done, but I can always get my words out fine. I don't ever feel like I can't put a sentence together. 

I'm doing a good job explaining things today, right? I really want to make sure I'm giving you clear answers so I'm not making your job harder. I'm trying my best to be helpful.
Do you ever hear the voice when you are not at the shop?

Um... no, no, I don't. It's really just at the shop. I mean, that's the whole reason I came in to see you, actually. It's just... I'll be at work, and I keep hearing this man's voice. It comes right out of the garage vents, or... or sometimes when I'm checking an engine, it sounds like it's coming from right under the hood. 

And it's not like a mumble or anything, it's as clear as if somebody was standing right next to me. He just... he tells me things, like I shouldn't trust my husband, or that I can't touch certain cars that come in. But it's only there, I promise. Not at home or anywhere else. 

I know it sounds a little strange, but I'm being completely honest with you. It's okay that it's just at the shop, right? I mean, I'm really trying to handle it well and not let it bother anyone else. I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Have you experienced any traumatic events in your past?

Um... traumatic events? No, no, nothing like that. I had a really normal childhood, honestly. Just... you know, regular family stuff. Nothing bad. 

I mean, everyone has little bumps in the road, right? But definitely nothing I would call traumatic. I've always been pretty lucky that way, I think. I've always just tried to keep my head down, work hard, and be a good person. 

I'm sorry, I hope that's an okay answer. I know sometimes people come in here with really heavy, terrible things in their past, and I don't want to waste your time since I don't have anything like that to report. I'm doing okay answering your questions, right? I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you hear the voice every time you're at the shop?

Um... no, not every single time. It's... it's just sometimes. 

Like I mentioned before, it's that man's voice, and it usually happens when I'm near the garage vents, or if I'm working under the hood of a car. It just sounds so real, like a customer or a coworker is standing right there, telling me I can't trust my husband, or that I shouldn't work on a specific car. But it's not all day, every day. I can still do my job, I promise. I don't let it get in the way of my work. 

I'm really trying to manage it, you know? I hope it doesn't make me sound... crazy or anything. I just wanted to be honest with you about why I made the appointment. Is it okay that it doesn't happen every single time? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right details.
Do you believe the voice is real and actually exists, or do you think it's just a product of your mind?

Um... well, that's... that's a hard question. I mean, I know why I'm here, and I know people probably think it's just my mind playing tricks on me. But... it just sounds so real. 

Like I said, the reason I came in is because I keep hearing this man's voice. It comes right out of the garage vents, or from under the hood when I'm working, and it's as clear as if somebody was standing right next to me. And the things he says... telling me not to trust my husband, or that I can't touch certain cars... it feels so real when it's happening. 

But I'm here, right? I'm talking to you about it, so I guess part of me knows it's... maybe not right. I don't want to sound like I'm completely out of touch with reality. I really am trying to be reasonable about this. I hope that makes sense. Is it okay if I'm not entirely sure? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answer.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports hearing a clear voice that provides instructions or opinions, which is a hallmark symptom of a psychotic disorder. The voice is not constant and is typically triggered by specific environments (e.g., the garage at work). The patient does not report any significant impairment in social or occupational functioning due to the voice, but there are some minor issues with relationships and work performance. The patient's symptoms do not meet the full criteria for schizophrenia, as there is no evidence of disorganized speech, catatonic behavior, or negative symptoms. Therefore, a diagnosis of acute and transient psychotic disorder (F23) is more appropriate.
